item.title: West Ham interested in signing Arsenal youngster who is out on loan
item.description: West Ham interested in signing Arsenal youngster who is out on loan Ethan Nwaneri is facing an increasingly difficult situation at Borussia Dortmund, where he is spending the current season on loan . His future in Germany is now uncertain, with the possibility that his temporary spell could be brought to an end in January. Should that happen, the young midfielder already has a potential destination, with another club reportedly prepared to bring him into their squad for the remainder of the campaign. A move could provide him with an opportunity to regain his confidence and secure more regular playing time. Nwaneri is regarded as one of the finest young talents in the Arsenal squad and among the club’s most promising academy graduates in recent years. However, he is currently struggling to establish himself, both at the Emirates and during his loan spells away from North London . West Ham emerge as potential destination The youngster spent the second half of last season on loan at Olympique Marseille. His time in France initially showed considerable promise, but his situation deteriorated as the campaign progressed. A similar pattern appears to be developing during his current spell in Germany, raising questions about whether another change of environment would benefit his development. Despite these difficulties, Nwaneri will be hoping to turn his situation around and demonstrate his considerable potential. Arsenal, however, want him to play regularly and continue developing, which could prompt the club to consider recalling him when the January transfer window opens. West Ham have emerged as a possible destination should Arsenal decide to end his loan spell at Dortmund. According to Football365 , the Hammers regard Nwaneri as a valuable addition who could strengthen their squad for the remainder of the season. (Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images) Loan move could offer fresh opportunity West Ham are keen to secure promotion back to the Premier League and believe that bringing in a player of Nwaneri’s quality could improve their chances. They are reportedly interested in signing him on loan for the second half of the campaign. Such a move could prove beneficial for the Arsenal youngster, particularly if it provides him with the regular opportunities he has struggled to secure in Germany. More consistent involvement would allow him to rebuild his confidence, gain valuable experience and demonstrate his abilities. For Arsenal, finding the right environment for Nwaneri’s development will remain important. A January move to West Ham could offer a practical solution for all parties. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Serena Williams’ former coach has noticed two big changes in Alexander Zverev as he becomes world number one
item.description: Alexander Zverev finally reached the summit of the ATP rankings after years of being a nearly man in men’s tennis. Zverev had cemented his status as the greatest player never to win a major up until Roland Garros earlier this season, where he secured his first Grand Slam title. After his triumph in Paris, the German reached his first Wimbledon final before clinching major number two at the US Open and ultimately becoming the world number one, rising above injured Jannik Sinner. Photo by Daniel Kopatsch/Getty Images Patrick Mouratoglou explains how Alexander Zverev has improved Zverev has faced criticism from pundits and fans alike since becoming the world number one, with some claiming he doesn’t deserve to sit atop the rankings due to his poor record against top-ten players and being winless against Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner in 2026. Others have come to the defence of Zverev, however, including Serena Williams’ former coach Patrick Mouratoglou. In a post on Instagram , Mouratoglou said: “Is Zverev better now than he was one year ago? Oh yes. “For two reasons. First, his serve has progressed a lot. It’s huge now; huge! The percentage of first serves is huge, the accuracy is huge, the speed is huge, the second serve is huge, everything is huge. “Secondly, yes, he is not the guy who has the ability to accelerate suddenly and make a big difference like Alcaraz, but if you look at the pace of the rallies, I think that Zverev is playing way faster than he was one year ago, and the big reason for that is because of his position. “He was two metres behind the baseline, and now he is just behind the baseline. He didn’t do this overnight, but he worked on it a lot to be able to position himself way closer to the baseline, and he still doesn’t make a lot of unforced errors, so he is super consistent while playing very close to the baseline at the same pace as before. So technically, because he is closer to the baseline, the rhythm of the rallies is way higher than before.” Zverev became the first German player in men’s tennis to reach the top of the rankings since Boris Becker in 1991. He also set the record for the fewest titles won by a year-end number one in a season with two.

item.title: 'He will win games single-handedly': Ex-cricketer backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World Cup
item.description: Former India captain and chief selector Kris Srikkanth has thrown his weight behind teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, backing him for opportunities across formats and urging the Indian team management to consider him for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm with his extraordinary batting performances, showcasing remarkable power, timing and confidence at such a young age. Impressed by the youngster's fearless approach, Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi has the potential to become an all-format cricketer and should not be restricted to a particular format. Speaking on his YouTube channel, the former India opener also suggested that the teenager should be considered for the upcoming ODI series against Sri Lanka. Kris Srikkanth backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World Cup Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi deserves to be included in India's 15-member squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup, even if the team management is not yet convinced about his readiness for Test cricket. The former India selector stressed that the youngster should be given opportunities in the 50-over format to help him develop and gain experience at the international level. "He is an all-format player. You don't want to play him in Tests, okay, but at least keep him in the 15. There is no questioning now. Sri Lanka will be coming for ODIs, give him a chance there. Put him in and let him play ODIs against them. If you really want to develop Suryavanshi, take him to the 2027 World Cup. Let him be in the 15. One day he will win you games single-handedly," Srikkanth said on his Youtube Channel. Srikkanth compares Sooryavanshi with Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli Drawing comparisons with two of India's greatest batting icons, Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, Srikkanth went a step further by describing Sooryavanshi as the "son of the god of cricket". "The way he is batting, power alone is not enough. You need timing as well. It is not just about power, it is also about his confidence. He looked so still and calm. He does not look ruffled. The greatest thing is that he knows exactly what he is doing. This is genius. First came the god of cricket, Sachin Tendulkar, then the King Virat Kohli, and now he is the son of the god of cricket," he said. "If you do not encourage this guy and keep saying that he has to be groomed, it is unfair. You are going to spoil a cricketer this way. Team management and selectors, please wake up," he added.

item.title: Bass 57-Yard Kick Saves Bills In Rainy Chiefs Loss
item.description: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost a tight game on Thursday night in Buffalo, and the reason was simple. Tyler Bass hit a 57-yard field goal as time expired to lift the Bills past the Chiefs, 13-10. It was a single kick in the rain that ended the night. Fans who watched the game know how much this hurts. The team fought hard but fell short because of one play at the very end. Rainy conditions made the night hard for both teams to handle. The weather played a big role in how the game went down. Syracuse.com states that a clutch kick by Tyler Bass secured a Bills victory over the Chiefs despite the rain. The field was slick and the air was wet, creating huge pressure. Bass did not miss. He put the ball through the uprights when the clock hit zero. It is a brutal way for a rival team to win, but it is also a sign of how tough the Bills are. The Scoreline Tells The Story The final score was 13-10, a low number that shows how hard the defense played. Yahoo Sports reports the Bills defeated the Chiefs via a deflected punt and a 57-yard field goal by Tyler Bass as time expired. A deflected punt set up the final play, and the kick sealed the deal. The Chiefs had chances to win or tie, but the rain and the Bills’ defense held them back. It was a game where every yard mattered. The offense could not find a rhythm in the wet conditions, and the special teams had to carry the weight. Bass did his job perfectly. A Hard Loss For The Kingdom This loss stings because it was so close. The Chiefs are used to winning these types of games. They have a history of coming back in the fourth quarter. But this time, the clock ran out before they could make their move. Per KY3, Tyler Bass sank a 57-yard field goal at the buzzer to help the Bills edge out the Chiefs. The Bills won because Bass made a big kick. There is no other way to explain it. The Chiefs will have to deal with this loss and move on to the next game. The team needs to fix the issues that let the Bills win in the final seconds. The rain made it hard, but the kick was the difference.

item.title: Decisive clash: Liverpool and Racing seek a place in the Uruguayan final
item.description: Decisive clash: Liverpool and Racing seek a place in the Uruguayan final Today brings a huge occasion in Uruguayan football: Liverpool and Racing battle for a place in the Uruguayan Championship decider, where Peñarol are already waiting for their opponents. The match takes place today at 20:30 at the Campus de Maldonado. Both teams arrive as winners of the season's short tournaments: Racing as Apertura champions and Liverpool as Clausura champions. Both want to keep dreaming of the ultimate glory: lifting the trophy as 2026 Uruguayan champions. Racing won the Apertura for the first time in their history with 31 points: 9 wins, 4 draws and 2 defeats. Chambián 's side could not maintain their winning form for the rest of the year, having lost several key players after the Apertura. Agustín Álvarez Wallace, Felipe Cairus and Thiago Espinosa were among the stars who moved elsewhere. The Brewers are seeking victory today to continue writing the story of the best year in their history. Liverpool , meanwhile, will contest the semi-final after being crowned Clausura champions. Under Fossati, who transformed the team, they earned 33 points and claimed their 11th official title since 2019. This is a team that has been in the mix for seven years, challenging for major honours almost every season. Today in Maldonado, they will look to overcome Chambián's side in their quest for a second Uruguayan Championship title. Belvedere against Sayago, Chambián against Fossati, the Black and Blues against the Brewers, the Little School against the Talent Factory; the dream of a first triumph against the hunger to reach the heavens once again. item.title: Players Era Recap: What we learned, and questions for the future
item.description: Jaquan Johnson #11 of the Iowa State Cyclones celebrates against the St. John's Red Storm during the first half during the Third Place game in the Players Era 16 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at Michelob ULTRA Arena on November 27, 2026 in Las Vegas. | Brandon Hooten/Players Era Through the first two weeks of the non-conference slate, there were many questions that surrounded this year’s edition of Iowa State men’s basketball. After dropping their season opener against Memphis, the Cyclones picked up three victories against admittedly weak competition with Southern Miss, Southern and Niagara. Just by the scoreline, none of those wins look particularly alarming. But those who watched the games live would tell a different story. There were a noticeable amount of missed rotations, which everyone should expect with the amount of minutes being given to the various transfers. My biggest concern throughout was the subpar three point shooting. The Cyclones entered Las Vegas connecting on just 24% of their three point attempts. It doesn’t take a rocket scientist to know that won’t cut it, and would also likely improve due to the law of averages. I would also not be the only person to express some individual concerns. Jamarion Batemon was ice cold from beyond the arc, going 5-27 in the first four games, including 0-7 through his first two games. After scoring 12 points against Memphis, Tamin Lipsey failed to score in double figures in the three home games. Blake Bucchanan looked much more sluggish throughout, which likely caused the switch to Dominykas Pleta into the starting lineup. After a full week of preparation, would any of these questions be answered in Las Vegas? Eh. While I would typically use the rose and thorn format for performances, we will change the format to pumpkin pie and cranberry sauce (I have no idea how some of you can eat this, fight me). Pumpkin Pie and Cranberry Sauce Vs. SDSU Their first bout against the Aztec was a solid enough outing against a squad that was picked to finish third in a new Pac-12 conference. The difference would ultimately be decided early with Iowa State notching a 10-0 early to take a 17-10 lead. That would be the only “kill shot” (any unanswered run of 10 or more points) for either team as the margin stayed between 6 and 10 for much of the afternoon. Pumpkin pie: Defensive fundamentals. The famous Otzelberger defense forced 18 turnovers, the second highest total of the season behind an absurd 30 for Southern. Even when the Aztecs were able to put up shots, they struggled through 38% from the field and 23% from distance. Pumpkin pie: Tre “Ole reliable” Singleton 22 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 steals? Solid day at the office. That performance earns first serving at the team dinner. item.title: No. 7 Miami Seniors Face Bittersweet Farewell Against Boston College
item.description: Credit USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Saturday marks a hard stop for the old guard at Hard Rock Stadium. The No. 7 Miami Hurricanes host Boston College for their final regular-season home game, and the atmosphere feels heavy with history. This is the last chance for players who spent their entire college careers in Coral Gables to say goodbye on home turf. It is a rare moment in a modern era where most players jump to the NFL after one or two years. The team stands at 10-1 with a perfect 8-0 record in the ACC, but the emotional stakes for the seniors are just as high as the playoff hunt. Senior defensive lineman Ahmad Moten Sr. knows the clock is running out. He spent five years building this defense and now faces the end of the line. “It’s definitely going to be a bittersweet moment. Last home game, last regular-season home game at Hard Rock … I’m not going to cry, of course, but it went by quick,” Moten said, according to Sun Sentinel . He admitted he didn’t believe his teammates when they warned him time would fly. Now he sees it all happened in a blink. The feeling is shared by running back Mark Fletcher Jr., who plans to savor every second before the final whistle. Standard of Play Must Stay High While the seniors get their flowers, head coach Mario Cristobal wants the team to keep playing with fire. The defense looked great against Virginia Tech, but the coach wasn’t happy with the slow start. Cristobal demands consistency from the first snap to the last. “We’ve got to play to our standard,” Cristobal said after the game, according to Sun Sentinel . He wants the speed and aggression seen in the final minutes to be there from the very beginning. That kind of intensity cannot be a switch that players flip only when the game is on the line. The coach believes the team needs to hunt down the quarterback with the same drive they showed late in the last contest. “That can’t be a switch because that is a different — if you watch it — it’s a different level of acceleration, hunting down the quarterback,” Cristobal said. The players agree that they need to fix their early-game lapses. Ahmad Moten Sr. told the team they must own their mistakes and get right. The defense gave up a long drive on the first possession against Virginia Tech but held the Hokies to just 133 yards after that. The goal is to make that strong finish the new normal. Recruiting Wins While Roster Turns Over Even as the current class finishes up, the program is already winning the next battle. To lock in the nation’s leading 2027 recruiting class, Miami secured five-star defensive end DJ Jacobs, flipping him from Ohio State. The move puts the Hurricanes ahead of every other school in the rankings. No other squad can equal Miami’s current total of seven five-star prospects within its class. This depth ensures the team will remain competitive long after the current seniors hang up their cleats. The program is also still active in recruiting trails. Four-star linebacker Quinto

item.title: Giants Must Avoid 49ers, Bears And Vikings In 2026 Playoffs
item.description: New York Giants place kicker Dominic Zvada (34) successfully kicks a field goal during a week 11 NFL football game between New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Following a strong victory against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the New York Giants sit comfortably atop the NFC East with a 6-3-1 record. GMEN HQ identifies three specific NFC contenders that Big Blue should dread facing in the 2026 playoffs. The San Francisco Juggernaut The San Francisco 49ers stand as the best team in the entire NFL right now. Even with numerous injuries and an older roster than most in the league, this squad continues to dominate. Brock Purdy leads the offense as an MVP contender while Kyle Shanahan calls the plays. According to GMEN HQ, San Francisco will probably secure the NFC’s No. 1 seed. The Giants might not meet them until the championship game, but a January clash remains a real possibility. A Chicago Offense That Dominates The Chicago Bears rank as the second-best team in the conference and are legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Their offense ranks eighth in the NFL in total yards per game and scoring per game while holding the league’s top rushing attack. Quarterback Caleb Williams is having an exceptional 2026 campaign with a career-best 68.3% completion rate. He also posted a solid 95.9 passer rating during this strong season. To strengthen the unit further, the Bears defense brought in Jeffery Simmons, a Pro Bowl pass rusher from the Tennessee Titans. A Minnesota Defense Built To Win The Minnesota Vikings possess a championship-caliber defense led by coach Brian Flores. The Giants offense has struggled to find its identity since losing Jaxson Dart back in Week 2. A playoff matchup against Minnesota would test the Giants’ current attack. The Vikings have lost to the Giants before. The Giants face the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium for their next game.

item.title: Suns’ Miles Bridges is ‘good now’ after injury scare vs Rockets
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Erik Williams-Imagn Images Suns’ Miles Bridges is ‘good now’ after injury scare vs Rockets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Concern crept into the Phoenix Suns ’ roster during Wednesday’s 116-104 loss to the Houston Rockets. The most concerning element had to be a potential Miles Bridges injury. He tweaked his ankle during a second-quarter post-up with Alperen Sengun. Bridges subsequently fell on top of him after Sengun was fouled on the play. The Phoenix forward only played 26 minutes, and signs of a potential injury were there. He wasn’t moving the same way he usually does. There wasn’t the same amount of bounce and pep in his step moving up and down the court. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Although Bridges and the Suns were riding high during the road trip, this potential injury was a question mark. Luckily for the fanbase, he clarified his current condition ahead of Friday’s game against the Dallas Mavericks. “It was the 2nd quarter when (Alperen) Sengun tried to post up on me, and I pushed him, and he kind of flopped, and I fell over him,” he said via AZCentral’s Duane Rankin on X (formerly Twitter). That’s when I kind of tweaked it. I couldn’t move the same way the whole game, but I’m good now.” Miles Bridges can make an impact for Suns vs Mavericks The recently acquired Phoenix forward leads the team in rebounds per game (7.4) and is the third-leading scorer. Not to mention, Bridges’s playmaking has been impressive , averaging the second-most on the team (3.7). His downhill and driving ability is always a guarantee, but when the shot is falling, that’s when he’s at his most dangerous. That being said, there are still some concerns that he can address with his team. The rebounding is a byproduct of the team’s lack of size, but also not handling physicality the best. Facing off against Cooper Flagg and the Mavericks can be a good test for observing their own physicality. For them to win, it needs to match up and be elevated. item.title: Charles Leclerc explains Qatar GP practice spin after painfully "slow" day for Ferrari
item.description: Motorsport photo Charles Leclerc rued a "very, very difficult" FP2 for Ferrari at the Formula 1 Qatar Grand Prix, with his early spin the symptom of a general lack of grip in the SF-26. Having already gotten off to a quiet start in FP1, Leclerc and team-mate Lewis Hamilton could only manage seventh and eighth in FP2, a full second adrift of Mercedes' leader Kimi Antonelli . Read Also: F1 Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli leads Mercedes charge in twice red-flagged FP2 Not helping his cause, Leclerc suffered a violent spin exiting Turn 7 in the early stages of the session, sustaining floor damage that warranted a parts change mid-session. Leclerc explained that he had actually already damaged his floor earlier in the session over Lusail's notoriously high kerbs, and further damage following his excursion through the gravel trap forced Ferrari to change the floor entirely. "It's been just a very, very difficult session." Leclerc explained. "The best lap time was I think my first lap in FP2 and after that we could never really improve. Of course, we didn't do that many laps on the medium tyres because then we had to stop to repair because of the floor damage I got on the kerbs. "After I lost the car it probably made it even worse, so we just decided to change the floor which cost us quite a bit of time." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Ferrari sporting director Diego Ioverno explained: "After the spin there was clear damage on the floor. We saw it also from numbers, and we told him to stop. It was not repairable, so we replaced the floor. After that, there were still some small damages around the car, but nothing major." Leclerc didn't call in his floor damage as an excuse for the team's lack of pace, though, as also evidenced by Hamilton's poor pace as he reported a lack of rear grip. "To be honest, this is not even the reason why we were slow. We were just very slow from the first lap this morning to the last lap in FP2 and it's very difficult to understand what the outlier is," Leclerc acknowledged. With its many high downforce corners, motorcycle circuit Lusail is a track that the Ferrari SF-26 could have been expected to be competitive on, so the team is now poring over the data to find solutions overnight. "I really think there's an outlier that we need to find," Leclerc added. "At the moment, we just didn't quite put our finger on it, but we'll keep working in order to turn the situation around tomorrow. Overall, the pace has just been very, very poor. Low fuel, high fuel, normally high fuel is our strength, but today, there was just no pace at all. I don't really have an idea of what we can do significantly better that will turn the situation upside down." Ferrari also lost Hamilton to a power unit failure in the closing stages of an extended practice session, but as the seven-time world champion was running an older power unit for practice before turning to a fresher one overnight, his failure was not much of a concern, said Leclerc

item.title: Koepka’s Untucked Shirt Sparks Heated Golf Debate
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Brooks Koepka sparked a fresh debate over golf etiquette after appearing with an untucked Nike polo shirt during Friday’s Skins Game. The five-time major champion played at Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida, breaking a long-standing unwritten rule about professional presentation. While the PGA Tour strictly enforces tucked-in shirts at standard events and majors, this Black Friday exhibition operates outside those official regulations. The casual look immediately split the audience watching the Prime Video broadcast, proving that even entertainment formats have their own line in the sand. The Farmers Insurance Skins Game featured a $4 million purse and included Justin Thomas, Wyndham Clark, and rising star Jackson Koivun. Even though the occasion was laid-back, social media traditionalists immediately called the clothing sloppy and disrespectful to the game’s customs. Numerous people claimed that leading professionals ought to uphold standard presentation no matter the format. One X user opined, “Love Brooks but gotta tuck the shirt in,” while another wrote, “Brooks playing in the Skins Game with his shirt untucked is making my eye twitch.” A third viewer added that “Brooks is really not helping the apparel traditionalist with his designed untucked golf shirt,” according to GolfMagic . Some supporters of the 36-year-old noted that the Skins Game aims to be a relaxed, entertainment-first spectacle instead of a formal championship. This marks another instance where Koepka’s wardrobe selections attracted notice. At the Masters, Koepka has also donned collarless mock-neck shirts. Friday’s round marked Koepka’s debut in this specific exhibition format, yet his fashion choices continue to generate more conversation than his swing mechanics in some circles. The Clash of Tradition and Modern Style The reaction highlights a growing tension between golf’s rigid history and the modern player’s desire for individual expression. Golf has always been a sport where the clothes matter almost as much as the score, yet the lines are blurring. Koepka’s decision to wear a shirt designed to be untucked challenges the notion that a pro must look the same as a club amateur. The criticism from fans suggests that for many, the visual cue of a tucked shirt signals respect for the competition and the game itself. When that signal is missing, even in a fun event, it feels wrong to those who grew up watching the strict dress codes of the Tour. However, the Skins Game has always been an outlier in the golf calendar. It was created to be a high-stakes, low-pressure show where the rules are looser to encourage aggressive play. If the format allows for a relaxed vibe, why should the attire be different? Koepka, known for his aggressive play style, seems to be applying the same logic to his fashion. item.title: Celtics Must Win Friday To Secure Home Court In NBA Cup Playoffs
item.description: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics must win their Friday night game against the Atlanta Hawks to secure the top spot in NBA Cup Group C. A victory clinches the best record in the Eastern Conference for the tournament, which guarantees home-court advantage for the quarterfinals and semifinals. The stakes are high for a team that has traveled all month and needs to find its rhythm at TD Garden. Per The Boston Globe , the Celtics are 3-0 in the Cup with a massive plus-68 point differential, while the Hawks sit at 2-1 but could steal the top seed with a win. The Celtics have a clear path to the knockout round, but the Hawks are riding a four-game winning streak and are hungry to prove they belong. Atlanta has won eight of their last 10 games and is averaging 116.7 points per game, according to The Boston Globe. The Hawks also outscored their opponents by 29 points in the fourth quarter during their recent run. That late-game surge makes them a threat even if the Celtics build a big early lead. The Home Court Advantage Is Critical Playing at TD Garden is the key factor for Boston right now. The team has spent November on the road, and their play has sputtered due to the heavy travel schedule. Per CelticsBlog , locking up home court would allow the Celtics to regain a sense of normalcy and routine while they push toward the playoffs. The difference between hosting games in Boston and playing on the road in the quarterfinals is huge. If the Celtics lose Friday, they would still likely advance as a wild card, but they would face a harder road with away games for the next two rounds. Paul George addressed the team’s recent struggles after the win over the Wizards on Tuesday. He noted that the team had great looks but missed shots during their losing skid. “We shook the rust off,” George said. “We shot the ball with confidence.” The Celtics need that same confidence against Atlanta. Jayson Tatum led the team with 41 points in the last game, and he is averaging 27.3 points per game, which ranks fifth in the NBA. The Celtics’ defense is also a major factor, as they allow only 102.9 points per game compared to Atlanta’s 113.6. Injuries And Matchup Factors The Hawks are without center Jock Landale due to a hip injury and guard CJ McCollum because of a calf issue. Boston has its own concerns, as Mitchell Robinson is listed as questionable with an illness. Despite these absences, the Hawks have shown they can score in bunches, outscoring Detroit 33-12 in the final 12 minutes of their last game. The Celtics must stop Atlanta’s late-game runs to secure the win. Atlanta relies on perimeter defense and quick transitions, with Dyson Daniels proving to be one of the best defenders in the league. Boston relies on a balanced offense and superior shooting, hitting 36.2 percent from three-point range. The Celtics need to execute their offensive sets without turning the ball over. item.title: Man United make decision over Bruno Fernandes’ future
item.description: Man United make decision over Bruno Fernandes’ future Bruno Fernandes transfer latest as Manchester United move to protect valuation Manchester United are preparing for a significant decision on Bruno Fernandes, with the club understood to be moving to secure their position by triggering the one-year extension in his current deal. According to TeamTalk , that step would keep the Portugal international tied to Old Trafford until 2028 and, crucially, strengthen United’s hand if his future becomes a live transfer issue. The report suggests uncertainty around Fernandes has grown as United reshape under Mauricio Pochettino. There is a sense that internal planning is already taking place ahead of a major squad overhaul, and Fernandes, despite his status, has not been immune from that thinking. TeamTalk state that “Those close to the Portuguese superstar believe United are open to selling the 32-year-old” and that such a move could even come “as early as the upcoming January transfer window”. That is a striking claim when applied to a player who remains one of the defining figures in this United side. Fernandes underlined his enduring influence by scoring twice in the 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting CP, a reminder that even amid uncertainty, his output remains at an elite level. Contract option changes Manchester United stance What appears most significant is United’s reported decision to activate the extension option. TeamTalk say the club have “already informed Fernandes of their intention to trigger the one-year extension option in his current contract” and that this would “at the very least protect their valuation of a player they know remains in high demand.” In practical terms, it gives United leverage, whether the objective is to keep Fernandes longer or maximise any eventual fee. The background to this is a stalled negotiation over a fresh long-term agreement. The same report says talks have failed to gather momentum and that a recent proposal “falling short just two weeks ago” has only reinforced the impasse. Fernandes had reportedly wanted to stay until 2030, yet United’s hierarchy were unwilling to go that far. The gap between those positions has created uncertainty, even if both sides have publicly tried to keep the issue measured. It is also notable that while Fernandes has said he paused talks to focus on performances, TeamTalk add that “club sources insist the pause was a mutual decision given the previous stagnation.” That wording points to a situation with no immediate breakthrough in sight. item.title: 4 reasons why Seattle Seahawks can beat 49ers in Week 12
item.description: 4 reasons why Seattle Seahawks can beat 49ers in Week 12 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coming out of their Week 11 bye, the Seattle Seahawks get to go up against the red-hot San Francisco 49ers . It's not going to be an easy matchup by any means. That will likely be the case with their defense, as the Kyle Shanahan-led 49ers just had a massive week against the Minnesota Vikings ' elite defense in Week 11. So, it wouldn't be a surprise if this Seahawks defense struggled. However, there are four reasons why the Seahawks can beat the 49ers this week. ESPN Research and reporters Brady Henderson and Nick Waonger revealed the four key reasons why the Seahawks can beat the 49ers this weekend. 4 reasons why Seahawks can beat 49ers in Week 12 "The Seahawks are 2-0 off a bye week under Mike Macdonald, allowing an average of 15.5 PPG," ESPN Research shared. This key statistic for the Seahawks is one reason why they should have some confidence in their team's ability to beat the 49ers in Week 12. Mike Macdonald's teams have a lot of success coming off the bye, and that streak continuing this weekend wouldn't be a surprise, especially after the 49ers' big Week 11 win. But that's not the only reason why the Seahawks can beat the 49ers. ESPN's Brady Henderson highlighted how quarterback Sam Darnold is "on track to return" to his QB1 job this week after two weeks out due to a quad and rib injury. While there are some question marks surrounding Darnold's play this season, he helped them win the Super Bowl last season and is someone the Seahawks should have confidence in. MORE : Solving the Brian Flores puzzle: How Kyle Shanahan finally bested defensive guru in 49ers win 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner highlighted the two biggest reasons why Seattle might beat San Francisco in Week 12. They revolve around a key injury to right tackle Colton McKivitz and how good this Seahawks defense is. "Seattle's ferocious defense ranks fourth in pass rush win rate (55.6%) and seventh in pressure percentage (37.5%), and it sacked QB Brock Purdy three times in the first meeting," Wagoner writes. With the 49ers down their starting right tackle, facing off against a strong pass-rushing team that has already found success against a fully healthy 49ers OL this year, Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense might be in a little bit of trouble this week. Vederian Lowe will need to step up in a big way for the 49ers as the new right tackle. But, with how good the Seahawks' defense is, it would not be a surprise if he struggled. Even though the 49ers beat the Seahawks earlier in the year, with Darnold back, their strong matchup with a backup right tackle on the other side, and Macdonald's history coming out of the bye on their side, Seattle might be able to pull off the upset this week. item.title: Former IVC volleyball star returning to Purdue team for fifth year
item.description: Kenna Wollard is coming back. The Purdue volleyball All-American announced via social media on Friday, Nov. 27 that she will be back for her fifth season. Wollard, a three-time Journal Star Player of the Year, missed all of the 2026 season due to treatment for Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma. "I'll be back for my fifth year, and I'm so grateful I get to say that!!!!" Wollard posted on Instagram . "Thank you to everyone who's been in my corner. I love playing for Purdue, and I'm ready to give this program and my teammates everything I have next season." The 2023 Illinois Valley Central grad had revealed in October that her treatments for Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma were working and she was on track for remission. She was a first team All-Big Ten and second team All-American pick following the 2025 season. That season she posted 577 kills — third-most in program history. Wollard will be joined by Taylor Anderson, Big Ten all-conference first team, and Dior Charles, who also will be coming back for their fifth years. Purdue ended its regular season with a loss to top-ranked Nebraska in the Big Ten Conference Tournament semifinal. The Boilermakers, who have a 20-8 overall record, await their NCAA Tournament fate with Sunday's selection show. item.title: Blues Need Grit To Beat Stars In Tight Central Race
item.description: Joe Puetz-Imagn Images The Central Division is a mess, and the St. Louis Blues are stuck right in the middle of it. Dallas holds second place, but the gap to sixth place is just three points. That tiny margin means every single point matters. The Blues lost their four-game winning streak on Wednesday night in a shootout against the New York Islanders. Now they face a Dallas team that just saw its own five-game run end with a loss to Nashville. Both clubs are tired, but only one will survive Friday’s matchup in St. Louis. A Road Record That Matters Dallas has been nearly unbeatable on the road this season. Away from home, the Stars have posted a 6-1-2 record, having lost just once in regulation time. That is the fewest road losses in the entire league, per Field Level Media . It is a stat that hurts St. Louis right now. The Blues need to stop the bleeding if they want to climb the standings. A loss here would be a massive blow to their playoff hopes in such a crowded division. They cannot afford to let the Stars build a bigger cushion. Keys Missing for St. Louis The Blues are dealing with a nasty injury bug that could cost them the game. Forward Jimmy Snuggerud leads the team with 14 goals and 20 points, but he is out with an upper-body injury. Pavel Buchnevich is also listed as day-to-day due to a similar issue. These two players drive the offense, and their absence changes everything. Dallas coach Glen Gulutzan admitted his team was flat after losing to Nashville, noting, “This one is going to leave a sour taste in everyone’s mouth — players, coaches, everybody.” If the Blues can’t find a way to score without their top scorers, they will struggle against a Dallas defense that has been solid. Can They Bounce Back? St. Louis showed some heart on Wednesday when they forced overtime against the Islanders. Mason McTavish scored for the Blues, and the team showed they could compete even in a loss. “I loved our effort, I loved our grit,” St. Louis coach Jim Montgomery said after the game. He added, “I thought we played an intelligent road game.” The Blues need that same energy on Friday. They have a chance to prove they belong in the top half of the Central.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
